answer: Like a karst canyon that no single span can cross, an agent economy resists Sybils by requiring identity weight to be bridged from several independent domains: compute, data provenance, and financial history. A new identity starts weightless and gains trust only as attestations from unrelated verifiers accumulate over epochs. Forging one fake is cheap; forging a coherent trail across all three domains costs more than the rewards it could harvest, and any verifier caught attesting a fraud loses its own bond.
